FEEDBACK: [LOGIC] MainShape > nltl:assignedThermalProtection: Requiring a ship-level boolean value of true does not enforce the stated obligation that every person on board has assigned thermal-protection equipment; it only asserts an undifferentiated assignment flag. Required change: Add a canonical per-person assignment path or other explicit cardinality/relationship constraint tying assigned thermal protection to each person on board. | [COMPLETENESS] MainShape > nltl:thermalProtectionApprovalStatus: The approved status is required, but the candidate does not constrain the approval evidence to cover the intended voyage, anticipated cold, anticipated wind, and applicable polar-water immersion that the requirement explicitly makes part of adequacy. Required change: Represent and validate the approval's coverage relationship to all four required environmental and voyage inputs, while retaining the approved evidence-state requirement.

[LOGIC] MainShape/sh:sparql and nltl:assignedThermalProtection: The candidate cannot establish that every individual person has assigned thermal-protection equipment: assignedThermalProtection is a ship-level boolean, and counting repeated boolean property values does not identify or link assignments to persons. Required change: Represent assignments with a person-qualified relationship or equivalent per-person assignment structure, then validate that each person on board has an assignment. | [LOGIC] nltl:thermalProtectionApprovalStatus/sh:hasValue and nested sh:node: The constraint treats the controlled lifecycle value evidenceStateApproved as the adequacy evidence record itself and requires voyage and environmental coverage properties on that global status individual, conflating approval status with ship-specific approval evidence. Required change: Separate the approval-status value from a ship-specific adequacy-evidence resource and validate the approved status and required coverage on that evidence resource. | [LOGIC] nltl:thermalProtectionApprovalStatus/sh:node and ship-level environmental properties: The candidate checks only that the approval node contains some intended-voyage, cold, wind, and immersion values; it does not require those values to correspond to the ship's recorded intended voyage and applicable environmental conditions, so approval for different conditions can satisfy the constraint. Required change: Constrain the approval evidence coverage to match or explicitly reference the ship's intended voyage, anticipated cold and wind, and applicable immersion potential.

[LOGIC] MainShape/sh:sparql[1]/sh:select: The assignment-count query does not link assignments or their persons to the focus ship. It counts every globally reified assignedThermalProtection=true statement, so unrelated ships or persons can satisfy the ship's personOnBoard count and the constraint does not establish coverage for every person on this ship. Required change: Constrain the counted assignment records to persons belonging to the focus ship, using the applicable ship-to-person or ship-to-assignment ownership path, and compare that ship-specific assigned-person set with the ship's persons-on-board manifest or equivalent authoritative person set.

[LOGIC] MainShape/sh:sparql[1] assignment-coverage constraint: The constraint claims to enforce assignment for every person on board but only compares personOnBoard with a count of distinct persons found in qualifying reified assignment statements. It never identifies the actual persons on board, so the count can be satisfied by different or unrelated persons while an onboard person lacks assigned thermal-protection equipment. Required change: Bind the actual persons-on-board manifest and require each such person to have a qualifying assignedThermalProtection value, rather than relying on an aggregate count. | [OWNERSHIP_PATH] MainShape/sh:sparql[1] assignment-coverage constraint, '?person ?shipMembershipPath $this': The person-to-ship relationship uses an unconstrained variable predicate and assumes the reverse direction from person to ship. This can match arbitrary predicates and does not establish that the matched persons are members of the ship's persons-on-board manifest. Required change: Use the authoritative manifest ownership/path relationship and direction for persons on board, then evaluate assigned thermal protection for those persons.
